title: Waves Integrity Audit Schema
description: Structured report produced by the logbook integrity reviewer (logbook-create Step A6). One per audit run, persisted alongside the logbook so the second-order corpus miner (w6 Phase 5) can read it across logbooks/projects.
$comment: CANONICAL SHAPE: a single object with keys logbook_path, audited_at, model, summary, findings. OPEN (never additionalProperties:false, design_principle #11) — a recurring extra key is a signal for the corpus miner, not an error. STOP: one audit run per file (the reviewer overwrites on re-audit; copy first if history is needed). REDIRECT: the fixes the main agent applied go in the logbook's recent_context, NOT here — this file is the read-only finding record. An undeclared sibling field is the signal you are writing the wrong artifact. bad: adding an 'applied_fixes' array here (that belongs in the logbook). good: summary {critical, warning} + findings[] each citing primary_id/secondary_id.

logbook_path.description: Repo-relative or absolute path of the audited logbook.

audited_at.description: UTC timestamp of the audit run.

model.description: Model or agent that produced the audit.

summary.description: Compact counts for quick reading; full detail is in findings.

findings.description: One entry per finding. An empty array means the logbook passed clean.

finding.description: A single integrity finding against the logbook.
finding.$comment: STOP: one issue per finding — cite the structural element (primary id, secondary id). REDIRECT: the fix narrative belongs in the logbook recent_context, not in `message`; do not bundle unrelated omissions. bad: one finding listing three different missing-rule problems. good: one category + one location + one cited message + one suggested_action.

severity.description: Only these two. If it does not reach 'warning', omit it.

category.description: Finding category, e.g. missing_rules_in_primary, coverage_gap, decomposition_mismatch, edge_case_empty_expected.

suggested_action.description: Textual suggestion; do NOT prescribe exact JSON edits — the main agent decides how to apply.
